chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said:

The daughters of the daughter stand in the place of the daughters if the deceased has no daughters and no other heirs than them, and the daughters of the son stand in the place of the son if the deceased has no children and no other heirs than them.
And from him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The daughters of the daughter inherit if there are no daughters who stand in the place of the daughters.
And what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Safwan, from Khuzaymah ibn Yaqtin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The son of the son, if there is no one from the man's loins, stands in the place of the son. He said, and the daughter of the daughter, if there is no one from the man's loins, stands in the place of the daughter.
And what al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah also narrated from Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: The daughter of the son is closer than the daughter of the daughter.
And what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the son of the daughter and the daughter of the son. He said: Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) did not spare [effort] in giving the inheritance to the closer one. I said: Which of them is closer? He said: The daughter of the son.

These narrations are not acted upon by the consensus of the True Sect, because we have clarified that with the daughter of the loins, the daughter of the daughter and the son of the son do not inherit, and each of them stands in the place of the one through whom he is connected, if there is no one there who is closer. And as for the last two narrations and what they contained that the daughter of the son is closer than the daughter of the daughter, they are also not sound, because their degree is one, and it is that each of them is connected through the one who is connected to himself, so their closeness is one. The way with these narrations is to carry them upon a type of precautionary piety (taqiyyah), because among the general public is one who goes to that.

ai.seo_question: How do granddaughters and grandsons inherit in Shia jurisprudence when direct children are absent?
ai.summary: This passage from *Al-Istibsar* details the Shia jurisprudential debate regarding the inheritance status of grandchildren (*awlād al-awlād*), specifically addressing whether they inherit alongside or replace direct children. It highlights the tension between narrations suggesting granddaughters inherit with daughters and the dominant view that they only inherit in the absence of direct offspring, a discrepancy often explained through *taqiyyah* to reconcile with Sunni practices. The text also clarifies the principle of proximity (*qurb*) in inheritance, noting that the daughter of a son is considered closer than the daughter of a daughter, reflecting the Shia emphasis on patrilineal descent.
